lines: Mind the smokehouse. What do you need?
Step clear of the smokehouse. What do you need?
Mind the smokehouse. I am listening.
You caught me between the chopping block and the smoker.
Come around the clean side of the table and speak.
I have a moment before this batch needs turning.
If this is about supper, you are early. If it is trouble, start talking.
Stand clear of the hooks and tell me what happened.
I just washed my hands, so your timing is better than usual.
You look worried enough to put me off my lunch.
Give me the important part before the smoker calls me back.
I was counting the winter stores. Try not to make me begin again.
If you need something wrapped, wait until I finish listening.
The cleaver is down and the door is open. Go on.
I know that look. Something has gone bad, and it is not the meat.
Speak plainly. Smoke and riddles both get in my eyes.
You made it here in one piece. Let us keep it that way.
I can clear a stool if this will take longer than a minute.
Is this about work, danger, or somebody touching my hooks?
The day has already been strange, so you may as well add to it.
